<!-- pr-reviewer: 1ddaa944abaa298fb4d2423782000c229d208336 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge** (with the note below on hands-on 4th-axis verification).

### What looks good
- Both changes are narrow and rotary-wrap-only: `air_levels` (entry.rs) counts a plane within `EPS` of the leave limit as material, and `hsm::narrowed_helix` refuses a narrowed helix by name (`NARROW_HELIX`) before planning, falling back to Offset rings with a note (`hsm.rs`, seam-gated). Planar paths are untouched.
- Prime Directive: the safe direction. The overloaded narrowed spiral is replaced by a named refusal and the proven Offset-rings path; the r6.2 travel refusal is kept and pinned by name. No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests; `choose_entry` errors are not swallowed (the planner re-asks and names its own refusal).
- Pinning tests exist for each behaviour; test file split brings files under 400 lines (hsm.rs 321, rotary_adaptive.rs 306); decision record present; body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #55`; no CHANGELOG/RECOMMENDED edits; no build.rs, scripts, workflows or dependency changes.

### Local results (merged with current main, own target dir)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-motion --lib` | 155 passed |
| `rotary_adaptive` (debug) | 2 passed, 3 heavy ignored |
| `rotary_adaptive --ignored` (release) | 3/3 passed, incl. `adaptive_plans_the_developed_levels_under_the_load_and_kink_laws` (140 s) |
| `rotary`, `rotary_offset`, `rotary_links`, `rotary_dflat`, `pocket3d_hsm` | 10 / 9 / 7 / 7 / 3 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (not blocking)
- This changes posted 4th-axis output (levels at the leave limit now take two laps; narrow Adaptive bands now use Offset rings). No hands-on machine/simulator check was possible per the PR; the maintainer should judge that.
- The 19.5 % vs 19.7 % load margin on the r7 bar is thin, as the PR itself says.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
